key_insight: Some classically polynomial-time graph properties cannot be computed by polynomial-size symmetric quantum circuits with entanglement width o(n/log n), even at unrestricted depth.
engineering_relevance: For symmetry-preserving quantum designs, circuit size alone is insufficient: limited entanglement width can prevent efficient computation of otherwise tractable graph properties.
method: Define entanglement width by the largest necessary state-factor block across layers and computational-basis inputs.
Use a partial-trace-based quantum pebble game to transfer classical indistinguishability lower bounds.
Construct polynomial-size symmetric circuits for BQP graph properties without entanglement restrictions and an efficient symmetric QAOA implementation for MAX 3XOR.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal lower bounds and constructive expressivity results, not empirical benchmarks or hardware evaluations.
watch_item: The lower bound applies to symmetry-constrained circuit families and does not establish an entanglement requirement for unrestricted quantum algorithms.
paper_title: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits
